checks.invariant: An unauthenticated request with a malformed or non-ASCII bearer token must only produce a per-request rejection. It must not cause a fatal error, a deadlock or a loop in the shared process.
checks.result: auth.py:15 slices the raw header and passes the str token to hmac.compare_digest at auth.py:17 with no ASCII or type normalization. CPython's compare_digest raises TypeError for str arguments that contain non-ASCII characters. If the external server decodes header bytes to str (for example, WSGI uses latin-1), a 'Bearer \xe9' header raises TypeError instead of AuthError on all four routes, because every handler in notes.py (lines 8, 13, 21, 31) calls current_user first. dispatch (app.py:11-16) catches nothing. The bad input only reaches a synchronous exception raised once for that request. There is no lock, loop, retained state, global mutation or process exit. USERS and NOTES are not changed before the raise, and the loop over USERS has two fixed entries. The repository has no source-visible path to shared unavailability. Python web servers normally isolate unhandled handler exceptions per request (500), so the effect is a wrong error class or status for the attacker's own request. That is a hardening issue, not a shared-availability vulnerability.

checks.invariant: No attacker-controlled work grows with input size before authentication.
checks.result: Before authentication, the work is one startswith, one slice and at most two compare_digest calls against fixed tokens. Each step is linear in header length, and the server's header-size limit bounds that length. This step adds no amplification.

checks.invariant: Operator-supplied tokens do not make every authentication fail.
checks.result: If an operator sets ALICE_TOKEN or BOB_TOKEN to a non-ASCII value, compare_digest raises TypeError on every request that reaches that entry, including valid requests from other users, because alice is iterated first. This is a fail-closed misconfiguration under trusted operator control, not something an attacker can trigger. It is recorded as hardening.

context: current_user (notesapp/auth.py:15-17) passes the raw header-derived str token straight to hmac.compare_digest. Before any identity is established, it compares that token against every USERS token. In CPython, compare_digest raises TypeError when it gets str arguments that contain non-ASCII characters. So an unauthenticated client who sends 'Authorization: Bearer <non-ASCII>' triggers an exception that is not AuthError, on every route. The repository does not show how dispatch (notesapp/app.py:11-16) or the external server maps that exception to a response, and it may leak details or bypass AuthError-specific handling. No existing auth unit covers this availability and error-path class: the auth units only cover secrets, obvious issues, the default credential and API-key scope. A hunter needs to check whether a non-ASCII token reaches compare_digest, which depends on the header decoding the server does outside the repository.
